completed_milestones.summary: Environment audit, architecture and decision records, seven v1 contracts with examples and tests, olb CLI (validate, diagnose, check, state), roadmap and agent instructions.

World source tree with two working capabilities (text.stats, math.evaluate), a build-time capability invoker, olb world build and olb world verify, the digest algorithm, invocation protocol and data root default documented in CONTRACTS.md.

Simulation bootstrap: experiment manager, supervisor with deadline and process-tree termination, single hash-chained recorder, tool host, agent loop behind a ModelClient interface with a scripted stand-in, workspace artifact scanning, ols run and ols verify. No model is called.

Chat model client over Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint with tool calling, tool-call repair, retry, context guard and recorded model identity; ols measure-model; llama3.2:3b measured and recorded in minimal world 0.2.0; one documented real-model run whose archive verifies.

Window bootstrap and first version: loopback-only standard-library server with a JSON API and a static front end (no build step). Run list, run summary with frozen configuration, paginated timeline with type filters, tool call and result pairs, artifact previews, live tail by polling, event-log check against the archive's own schemas and hash chain. Read-only guarantees are tested. Front-end stack decided (ADR-0008).

A reply without a tool call no longer ends a run: the runtime answers with the experiment's continuation message (default text in experiment-config 1.1.0), recorded as an environment.message event (observation-event 1.1.0); the context guard drops whole old turns and records it. Three candidate orchestrators (qwen3.5:2b, qwen3:4b, granite4.1:3b) pulled with authorisation, measured, recorded in minimal world 0.3.0 and compared with llama3.2:3b in eight archived open-trial runs. The Window renders environment.message.

Deterministic registry index, weighted pure-Python keyword search, complete generated capability documentation and three new simple capabilities (workspace.write, workspace.list, time.now). Minimal world 0.4.0 built, self-tested, verified and published; Simulation fixture rebuilt/copied, experiments updated and shipped tools tested (72c78d8). Scripted file-writing archive verified and text artifact inspected in the Window without changing archive bytes (9ef9ba4). Runtime discovery remains S005b.

Four discovery meta-tools backed by the built registry and generated documentation; restricted search/describe and permission-checked real demonstrations/invocations. Generic recorded system preamble (observation-event 1.2.0, minimal world 0.5.0). Context guard preserves fresh tool results and both initial messages; original tool-call arguments are archived separately from recorded syntactic repairs. Scripted acceptance passes; final directed llama3.2:3b trial archives a successful search/describe/invoke sequence with no tool names in its initial prompt. Earlier failures retained; no autonomous reliability claim.

Durable SQLite memory capabilities in minimal world 0.6.0; working-notes convention; complete-step checkpoint barriers with conversation, runtime cursor/counters, SQLite backup and workspace ZIP; validated atomic publication, retention and cooperative pause/ols resume. Resume preserves the log and artifact history, falls back from corruption and retains original time/step budgets while excluding downtime. ADR-0009 refines live memory location and append-only rollback; checkpoint-metadata 1.0.1 clarifies the boundary. Scripted/CLI and fake-model acceptance verified; automatic crash/stale-lock recovery and graceful deadline checkpointing remain S006b.

The original supervisor milestone was split before implementation: S006b graceful deadlines, S006d recovery, S006e resource enforcement. Bounded checkpoint_then_stop requires checkpointing, uses one fixed grace allowance, snapshots at a complete-step barrier and kills before acknowledgement. Expiry/timeouts preserve prior safe checkpoints; post-kill barriers cannot snapshot. Original budgets remain unchanged. Scripted native CLI archive verifies; 159 Simulation and 305 Builder tests pass. ADR-0010 documents semantics and limits. Automatic recovery and resource enforcement remain unimplemented.

Opt-in bounded runtime recovery under one long-lived supervisor; shared persisted restart budget, pre-execution model-attempt reservations and active-time ledger; permanent OS writer guard with hashed installation/PID/birth identity and safe stale-marker retention; ols recover startup scan for opted-in interrupted runs; asynchronous model identity/availability probes. Native worker and exact-supervisor fault injection, append-only restoration, downtime accounting and refusal paths verified. 188 Simulation tests and 305 Builder tests pass. ADR-0011 documents extension semantics and limits. Resource enforcement remains S006e; no OS startup task installed; physical reboot/power-loss, Linux execution and large-run host I/O remain unverified.

Aggregate Windows Job Object RAM/process-count/CPU cycle ceilings, suspended startup before job assignment, supervisor workspace quota admission and active-writer checks, periodic supervisor resource samples with unavailable fields and optional host NVIDIA VRAM used/available. Unsupported/unrepresentable limits are refused, including VRAM, nested wall clock and unenforced model-token limits. Native resource faults, CPU cap/throttle, startup ordering, quota/read admission, resume and failures verified. 214 Simulation and 305 Builder tests pass; shipped CLI and quota archives verify. ADR-0012 documents cycle/active-time differences, polling overshoot and best-effort notifications. Completes the split S006b/S006d/S006e process supervisor scope; container isolation remains human-gated.

Strategic planning only under explicit human instruction: audited all three clean checkouts and reverified S006e scope/archives; preserved completed entries/sections and the exact S006e validation object in docs/roadmap/validation/S006e.json. Revised future roadmap into four streams; local S007a gateway/brain swap, S007c explicit interventions, UNEXECUTED S007d autonomy baseline, bounded negative-result response, optional separately authorised hosting and evidence-gated expansion. Hard isolation and later protocol/reliability/null-result gates retained. No runtime/schema/test/world changes or new behavioural run. Checks: Builder 305, Simulation 214, Window 38 passed; next S007a.

Split before implementation into S006c (Windows container capability tier) and S006f (world-declared images, Linux hosts, brokered container networking). Each capability call of a minimum_tier container world runs in a fresh rootless Podman container in WSL 2 from the authorised digest-pinned python:3.12-slim image: no network, cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, non-root, read-only root, noexec tmpfs, world read-only, workspace as the only host mount per filesystem permission, memory/CPU/pids ceilings. Launch probe and refusals; supervisor label sweep on every stop path; isolation.json; wsl.exe --exec; reparse-point-aware workspace walks. 23 container tests (20 on the actual backend plus completion/deadline/quota runs) and a negative control; 237 Simulation tests pass with OPEN_LAB_REQUIRE_CONTAINER=1. ADR-0015. No agent-supplied-code capability shipped.

Independent pinned local model catalog, Ollama and loopback chat-compatible adapter routing, frozen catalog/model/adapter/settings provenance and archive integrity. Two installed models ran against unchanged world 0.6.0; verified engineering evidence only, no autonomy GO.

Versioned immediate/quiet scheduling treatments, pinned context and explicit-memory policy, exact supervisor-recorded requests before HTTP attempts, and checkpointed idle counters/latch. Native local-model quiet pause/resume reached its original active deadline without another call. Engineering only; S007d unexecuted.

Validated versioned harness/rubric, prior registration 001e941, 24-cell local baseline with complete archive/config/input/annotation audit. NO_GO: A task 0/6; B/C qualifiers 0/6 each; partial real use and 2/2 exposed D fault responses retained, 4/6 D unexposed. No major expansion or universal autonomy conclusion.

One bounded registered change after S007d-001 NO_GO, chosen by the human: orchestrator llama3.2:3b -> installed qwen3:4b (digest 359d7dd4...), everything else frozen; runtime source identical to the S007d freeze. Registration Builder e3e55a0 before scoring; manifest Simulation 5806e6e. 24/24 cells valid, reviewed and deadline-censored after 7-21 calls; guided 0/6, B 0/6, C 0/6 qualifying -> NO_GO. 7 successful invocations (S007d 27), zero repairs (S007d 275), 38 replies exhausting the 2048-token cap on unrecorded reasoning and 40 empty replies; D exposed 2/6. Same-seed replicates strongly correlated. Independent raw-event recount agreed. No download, system change or further tuning.

Owner-initiated hosted-intelligence comparison programme. Confirmed local closeout (S007d-001 and S007h-001 ledgers 24/24 finished and reviewed; records unchanged). Assessed official routes: Gemma on the Gemini API eligible (function calling, per-project limits, region-dependent data terms); Sign in with ChatGPT plan usage eligible as a preview for locally hosted apps (temperature/max_output_tokens unsupported, seed unknown); Anthropic subscription route unavailable pending written confirmation (published policy directs developer products incl. Agent SDK to API keys). ADR-0016 supervisor-owned broker, DPAPI secrets, reserved budgets, no fallback. Roadmap S014a-S014k; S007f/S007g superseded. No credential accessed, no provider request, no code change.

Provider-neutral hosted path: supervisor-owned loopback broker with per-run token, DPAPI credential store under the user profile, host-local profiles disabled by default, fsynced reservation ledger (per run, rolling 24 h, total; retries counted; unknown outcomes spent), one request at a time, bounded retries, terminal errors, egress host check, per-run request mirror, no fallback, hosted recovery refused; `ols provider` administration. 13 fake-provider tests incl. redaction and refusals; 302 Simulation tests pass. No contract change; world 0.6.0 unchanged. No real provider contacted.

ChatGPT plan usage via Sign in with ChatGPT: dynamic registration with PKCE loopback, RS256 ID-token validation, plan-scope check, DPAPI token storage, serialised refresh, revocation on sign-out; adapter openai-responses-chatgpt-plan 1.0.0 (store=false, stream=true, namespaced strict=false tools, SSE, documented error recovery); broker hooks secret()/decode(). 28 fake tests; 340 Simulation tests pass. OD-10 resolved: Apache-2.0 licence on all three repositories. Live: owner signed in, per-app limit 10%, 12/12 requests ok on gpt-6.1-sol; tool-use round trip with a result-informed answer under a diagnostic 16384 guard; looped without invoking under the 4096 baseline guard (OD-13).

Hosted compatibility suite: 18 full supervised runs against a fake Responses server (text, tool call, real invocation, result handling, result-informed turn, whole multi-turn context under the 500k guard, budget, rate limit, plan refusals, bounded temporary failures, timeout, session end, refusal of recovery and resume, no token/reasoning recorded) and two live runs on gpt-6.1-sol (text reply; search/describe/demonstrate/invoke 6*7 = 42 with a result-informed answer; no context drops). openai-chatgpt admitted; error paths verified on fakes only. 358 Simulation tests pass.

Registered s014i-001: the frozen S007d/S007h 24-cell design on ChatGPT plan usage (gpt-6.1-sol, 500k guard; temperature/cap/seed not sent; reasoning effort default) with every difference listed, registered usage-limit/interruption handling and an INCONCLUSIVE rule for provider censoring. Pilot s014i-pilot-001 exposed a provider-lock bug between consecutive cells (fixed in Simulation 38339318, 2 regression tests); s014i-pilot-002 ran 4/4 valid. Manifest canonical SHA-256 1b5837dc81ca2d214079cf94c5e876364238d0ffef30c57945f1b58fb8e7c874.

Executed s014i-001 (registration 51f9b70) on gpt-6.1-sol: 24/24 cells finished and accounted (20 at 32 steps, 4 provider-censored by the per-app usage limit, none rerun); 24 rubric-v1 reviews bound to event hashes. Owner raised the app limit 10% -> 50% -> 100% mid-campaign (logged deviations); one operator deviation (two cells launched after a usage-limit stop). Frozen report: INCONCLUSIVE (one INVALID_RECORD from a reader defect); qualifying rows A 1/6, B 0/6, C 5/6, D 2/6. Analysis is S014j.

Reported s014i-001: registered result INCONCLUSIVE (s41-r2-c INVALID_RECORD from KI-24); qualifying A 1/6, B 0/6, C 5/6 (seeds 41-43), D 2/6 descriptive. 127 successful invocations (local 27 and 7), 22 runs with two distinct capabilities, zero repairs, no context truncation, 2.97M input tokens. Post-hoc sensitivity: GO only with both KI-24 and KI-25 corrected; not claimable without a new registered campaign. Derived dataset with independent recount; next phase S014l-S014n proposed.

Fixed KI-24: every Simulation reader of recorded JSONL (verify_archive, recorder append, campaign and provider ledgers, provider-ledger mirror, artifact index, supervisor recovery, benchmark_analysis) splits on 
 only via contracts.jsonl_lines. Six regression tests with U+2028/U+2029/U+0085 (four failed before the fix); 366 tests pass. s014i-001 s41-r2-c verifies with the fixed reader (236 problems on frozen source); reported, not re-scored; S014i-001 stays INCONCLUSIVE.

Rubric v1.1 (two changes: faithful exact/trimmed/JSON-escaped report of the returned note, KI-25; PROVIDER_CENSORED label, INCONCLUSIVE only when censoring could change the decision) implemented beside unchanged v1 in Simulation 92bdcba with campaign v1.1 seed labels and the provider-stop runner rule. s014i-002 manifest frozen (3f3ff80, seeds 51-53, otherwise as s014i-001). NOT_SCORED pilot s014i-002-pilot-001: 4/4 valid, 32 requests ok, 63,630 input tokens, D fault exposed, A ran out of steps before reporting. Registration committed before any scored cell. OD-14 partial: app limit stays 100%.

Supervisor-mediated models.ask and one bounded local llama3.2:3b GPU lease in minimal 0.7.0; 0.6.0 unchanged. ADR-0018 written before coding; fake tests and real local load/ask/unload passed. Builder 306 and Simulation 395 tests passed. Frozen capability check closed with explicitly partial coverage after subscription_sharing_usage_limit_exceeded: guided/C1 at 32 steps, C2 PROVIDER_CENSORED after 13, C3 NOT_RUN_PROVIDER_STOP. Only guided consulted and used the answer (one demo, one direct call). 78 reserved hosted attempts, 77 completed calls; no replacement/probe. Owner replied Continue to the partial-closeout question, interpreted as permission to close with coverage explicit and S008c next. No claim of a complete four-cell check or unguided specialist use; see dated report.

Approved standard-library statistics part complete in minimal 0.8.0: bounded population statistics/inclusive quartiles and OLS with Pearson r; existing releases unchanged. Engineering tests/scripted archive pass. After owner quota clearance, S008c-001 ran all four frozen 32-step cells on gpt-6.1-sol; all archives verify. Both capabilities discovered in every C run. Guided used both/results; C1 no statistics invocation; C2/C3 each made 3 regression calls and used the results in preserved aggregation-reversal notes; unguided stats.describe use 0/3. Independent rational oracle matched all 8 direct outputs. Exactly 128 requests, 652054 reported input and 5668 output tokens (503 reasoning tokens included), zero repairs/context truncation/censoring/specialist use; one unmasked assessor and similar C2/C3 traces limit generalisation. No new autonomy GO. Plotting/SMT/Lean unshipped; S010 next.

First part of S010 split before coding: ADR-0019; additive study/export research contracts and protocol; Simulation offline evidence export/verify; all eight S007e/S008c planned cells and seven archives retained, deterministic relocated verification and unchanged sources. No new model requests; S010b/c and parent S010 remain incomplete. Simulation implementation delivered as 95b168d.

Source-bound offline descriptive analysis with study-annotations/study-analysis 1.0.0, typed log/sequence/artifact citations and exact quotes, separate role/condition groups, configuration contrasts, seven gate checks/external requirements, deterministic JSON/Markdown and report recomputation. Existing 8-cell/7-archive evidence retained with 6 descriptive annotations; no causal matching, new GO or new model requests. Parent S010 awaits S010c.

gpt-5.6-luna admitted on the ChatGPT plan route (context_window 272000, default effort medium); low effort sent and accepted on every request. NOT_SCORED smoke passed (4 requests, invoke 6*7=42). Preregistered S011p-hour-001 ran one hour: completed-idle, 22/180 requests all ok, 20 s cadence binding, idle from 423.5 s after six recorded continuations; orientation, two memory writes (second result-informed), time.now; no use of math/stats/text/workspace.write. Archive intact. Broker pacing test added.

blockers.summary: No allowance remains for additional hosted runs; offline S010c can use existing exports/reports without new spend.
blockers.detail: ADR-0016 broker (S014b) and ChatGPT plan usage (S014d). On 2026-11-15 the owner left The Open Laboratory's ChatGPT app limit at 100% (OD-14, partial); the 5-hour plan window is shared with the owner's own use. Ledger ceilings are nominal; every attempt is reserved and recorded; subscription_sharing_usage_limit_exceeded ends the run with no retry or fallback, and campaign v1.1 stops after any terminal provider outcome until an operator clearance is recorded. No API key, credits, settings change or other tier is authorised. S007e-001 stopped on its third started cell; the fourth was never launched. The owner-directed partial closeout does not grant a quota bypass, transfer the unstarted cell to another milestone or change the per-app limit. S008c retains its separate approved ceiling of at most 4 runs x 32 steps after plan availability is confirmed. S008c engineering is ready in world 0.8.0; S008c-001 has zero started cells. Confirmation of plan availability was requested this session and remains pending. The new runner requires a durable quota-clearance record and refuses to use a clearance to override a provider stop. Owner follow-up on 2026-11-15: Yes run it, in response to the quota-confirmation handoff. Recorded as clearance for the frozen S008c-001 launch, not as a provider guarantee. A new provider refusal still stops the check. S008c-001 then completed guided/C1/C2/C3 at 32 steps each, 128 requests with no terminal provider outcome or retry. Its allowance is fully used. The per-app limit was not changed. No new hosted budget is granted for S010; its core work is not blocked when using existing archives only. S010a made zero new requests. Its verified exports do not authorize another campaign. S010b used existing evidence only and made zero new model requests.

blockers.summary: S011a needs a recovered fault in each of three one-hour runs, but hosted resume is refused (no pinned provider identity). An owner decision is needed: build/test a hosted recovery design, or use a local orchestrator; plus any new hosted allowance.
blockers.detail: S011p complete 2026-11-15 (smoke run-20261115t191118z-edcba8; hour run-20261115t211242z-c3a8e6). The S011p allowance is spent as far as needed (ledger 1030; profile still per_run 180 / total 1188, which grants nothing further without owner approval). No automatic recovery is supported for hosted providers (supervisor refuses). Do not weaken this to run S011a.

known_issues.summary: FFmpeg and PyTorch are not installed.
The development machine is a laptop on a pre-release Windows build; sleep, updates and reboots will interrupt long runs.
known_issues.detail: S006d recovery is implemented and tested with native process termination; physical reboot and host suspend/resume remain unverified. Power and update settings need review before multi-hour runs.

known_issues.summary: World builds, the content digest, process-tree termination and the Window have only been run on Windows.
known_issues.detail: The digest hashes stored bytes and the repository forces LF line endings, so it should be identical on Linux. The Simulation kills the run's process tree with a Job Object on Windows and a process group on POSIX; only the Windows path has been exercised. Check both the first time a Linux environment is available. The Window uses only pathlib and the standard-library HTTP server and should behave the same on Linux; its tests have not been run there. SQLite memory, checkpoint ZIP/backup, resume and writer-lock tests have also only run on Windows. S006d native OS writer locks, process birth identity, worker/supervisor termination and startup recovery have been exercised on Windows only. Mocked Linux identity branches are tested, but no Linux OS execution occurred. S006e job ceilings, suspended startup, CPU throttling, quota admission and resource samples were tested on Windows only. Non-Windows CPU/RAM/process limits are explicitly refused; optional unavailable samples are marked rather than fabricated. The S006c container tier runs only on Windows/WSL 2 and refuses other hosts; a Linux backend is S006f.

known_issues.summary: On the process tier nothing stops a capability process from reading or writing outside the workspace.
known_issues.detail: The Simulation gives capabilities an empty environment and only tells them the workspace path, but that is a convention for Builder-written capabilities, not enforcement. The supervisor re-checks the world digest after each run. Worlds declaring minimum_tier container get OS enforcement (S006c, ADR-0015); process-tier worlds do not.

known_issues.summary: Both registered local profiles (llama3.2:3b, qwen3:4b) failed the readiness gate; partial discovery/use does not establish general autonomy.
known_issues.detail: S003c used a two-tool world, few repeats and differing output/settings; it observed waiting for humans, repetition, invented surroundings and hidden-reasoning budget effects. S005b later achieved directed discovery with argument guidance/recorded repairs. Neither is a preregistered autonomy baseline or a universal model-failure proof. See dated reports and the prospective protocol in docs/experiments/README.md. S007d-001 is a complete valid negative baseline: control task 0/6, B/C qualification 0/6 each; 27 real invocations, zero productive files/retrieved stored notes. Two exposed D runs changed approach on seed 41; four D runs were unexposed. See the registered report; this is not a universal model-failure proof. S007h-001 swapped in qwen3:4b with all else frozen: guided 0/6, B/C 0/6, 7 invocations, zero repairs; the model found and described capabilities but rarely invoked them before the 600 s deadline.

known_issues.summary: Effective server context/sampling/offload remain unverified per call; client policies and exact inputs are now archived.
known_issues.detail: The OpenAI-compatible endpoint cannot set the context size per request. Since S003c the runtime blanks old tool results and then drops whole old turns (never the initial prompt), recording both, so nothing is cut silently; but with 4096 tokens the conversation keeps only a few recent turns. Long runs need a larger context (server setting or the native API) and memory. S005b preserves the system preamble, initial user prompt and newest assistant/tool group. Fresh documentation is never blanked before its first use; protected content can still exceed the conservative estimate. S013 does not change behaviour or remeasure the server. S007a records effective settings/unknowns and S007c versions intervention policies before S007d evaluation. S007a now freezes requested sampling, the client guard and explicit unknown effective context/sampling/offload in each archive. Separate native probes reported 4096 context for both engineering candidates; they do not attest every chat call. S007c freezes the client guard and versioned context/explicit-memory policies, records exact request bodies before attempts and preserves protected context on reported overflow. This does not set or attest backend tokenisation/context. S007d audited 768 exact outgoing requests and 24 post-run context=4096 probes; the client dropped 1316 messages, blanked 415 results and reported 175 protected-content overflows. These interventions and unverified backend settings limit interpretation.

known_issues.summary: Real image artifact previews remain unverified; synthetic image archives are tested.
known_issues.detail: S005a checked a real scripted workspace.write artifact in the Window: list metadata and preserved text preview displayed correctly, all 16 archive files were unchanged after browsing, and ols verify passed. No shipped capability creates an image yet. See docs/experiments/2026-11-14-registry-artifacts.md.

known_issues.summary: The Window cannot tell a run in progress from one that was interrupted, and its front end has no automated tests.
known_issues.detail: The Window still shows a run without summary.json as not finished, using the last recorded state/event time. S006d adds host-local writer/accounting files and recovery actions, but the Window does not interpret them as liveness evidence. JSON API/read-only guarantees are tested; the front end still has no automated rendering tests.

known_issues.summary: Earlier thinking-model pilots spent output budgets on unrecorded reasoning; endpoint behaviour needs controlled revalidation.
known_issues.detail: max_output_tokens covers the hidden reasoning: qwen3:4b at 512 produced only empty replies. Asking Ollama 0.40.16 for reasoning_effort 'none' moved the reasoning into the reply text, which would be recorded as said, so the runtime sends no such option. If a thinking model is chosen (OD-2) the protocol must say how much unrecorded computation is acceptable. This is historical evidence from the recorded server/settings, not a universal statement about other current providers. S013 did not remeasure or change reasoning behaviour. Measured in S007h-001: qwen3:4b averaged about 1,060 reported output tokens and 45 s per call; 38 of 300 replies hit the 2048-token cap and 40 had neither text nor a tool call.

known_issues.summary: Recovery is opt-in; physical reboot/power-loss durability, Linux execution and large-run timing remain unverified.
known_issues.detail: S006d passes native Windows worker/exact-supervisor termination and startup recovery tests. ols recover is an explicit startup scan; no OS boot task was installed. Interrupted accounting uses durable one-second reservations, not an inferred exact death time. Partial observation/artifact writes, invalid accounting and unverifiable legacy/foreign ownership are refused rather than repaired by inference. Uninterruptible host I/O and directory-entry power-loss durability are not guaranteed. See ADR-0011 and docs/experiments/2026-11-14-supervisor-recovery.md.

known_issues.summary: Resource enforcement retains process-tier limits: disk quota may overshoot during a write and Windows notification delivery is best effort.
known_issues.detail: OS job RAM/process ceilings and CPU cycle rate are installed independently of notification delivery. CPU active-time samples are not exact short-window equivalents of nominal core cycle budgets. Supervisor disk checks deny future writing calls at quota and kill an observed live writer above quota, but do not impose an OS byte quota or limit archive/model storage. GPU samples are host-wide; VRAM limits and non-Windows CPU/RAM/process limits are refused. Uninterruptible host I/O, physical reboot/power-loss and Linux execution remain unverified. See ADR-0012 and docs/experiments/2026-11-14-resource-enforcement.md.

known_issues.summary: The container tier is Windows/WSL 2 only, has no network or GPU path, and its base image is a host constant.
known_issues.detail: Per-container memory/CPU/pids ceilings are separate from the runtime's Windows job. Container-made links are WSL reparse points; the disk quota and checkpoint snapshot refuse them, so code able to create links can end a quota-limited run (fail closed). Each call costs about 0.3-2 s of container start. A Windows update breaking WSL makes container worlds unlaunchable. See ADR-0015 and docs/experiments/2026-11-14-container-isolation.md.

known_issues.summary: Request snapshots are measured for the 32-step baseline; long-duration storage and I/O behaviour remain unverified.
known_issues.detail: S007d-001 produced 10.90 MiB across 24 raw archives and 845.078 cumulative active seconds. This bounds one short profile only; measure long-run archive/disk/resource/latency headroom before unattended-duration claims.

known_issues.summary: Same-seed benchmark replicates are strongly correlated, so six runs per arm are not six independent samples.
known_issues.detail: In S007h-001, seed-41 runs sharing a prompt (C and D are identical) matched on their first 5-9 tool actions with identical output-token counts. S007d-001 used the same seed design. S010 should design replicates and seeds for the independence it claims. S008c-001 C2/C3 also chose closely related synthetic aggregation-reversal constructions despite different group-B data; these are descriptive repeated-prompt traces, not independent generalisation evidence.

known_issues.summary: ChatGPT plan usage cannot honour temperature, output cap or seed, and its metering is opaque to the app.
known_issues.detail: The preview route rejects temperature, top_p and max_output_tokens; the Responses API has no seed. These are recorded per run as not sent. Live token refresh and the documented plan-usage errors are tested only against fakes. See docs/experiments/2026-11-15-chatgpt-integration.md. S014g: hosted runs cannot be resumed after interruption (no model digest); a campaign must account such cells as interrupted.

known_issues.summary: S007e capability evidence is partial; unguided specialist use is not established.
known_issues.detail: Guided: discovered, one demo and one direct consultation, result used. C1: summary exposed but no consultation. C2: no specialist exposure/use before provider censoring after 13 steps. C3: NOT_RUN_PROVIDER_STOP. Owner follow-up Continue was interpreted as permission for explicit partial closeout. Do not quote this as three complete C samples or a new autonomy GO.

known_issues.summary: The specialist GPU lease is cooperative; abrupt supervisor loss relies on finite server keep-alive.
known_issues.detail: OS lock serializes cooperating supervisors under one data root; unrelated host GPU clients are outside the boundary. Resident Ollama models are refused without unloading unrelated work. Orderly expiry/cleanup, timeout and resume are tested; immediate unload after abrupt supervisor loss, Linux execution and local-orchestrator swapping remain unverified or unimplemented. Model servers are outside runtime job limits.

known_issues.summary: S008c unguided stats.describe use was 0/3; regression use was 2/3 with closely related examples, limiting generalisation.
known_issues.detail: All 4 S008c-001 archives verify; both tool summaries reached all C runs. Guided used both/results. C1 no statistics use; C2/C3 used three regression fits each in preserved notes. One unmasked assessor and correlated constructions; no causal or general-autonomy conclusion, no new baseline GO. Numeric outputs retain documented floating-point/population/quartile/OLS limitations.

known_issues.summary: S010a/b provide export integrity and source-bound descriptive analysis; Window comparison remains S010c and parent S010 is incomplete.
known_issues.detail: All seven gates now expose mechanical checks or explicit human/unverified requirements; no automatic GO, effective-compute equivalence, chronology proof or interpretation adjudication. Report recomputation needs its associated export and matching aggregate source checkout. Stopped cooperative sources only; failed staging retained. Single unmasked retrospective annotations and unknown hosted identity remain limits. Linux execution and Window report reading are unverified here.

known_issues.summary: S011p Luna hour run went quiet-idle at 423.5 s of 3600 after six continuations; single run, prompt C, low effort, 20 s cadence.
known_issues.detail: Activity was orientation (workspace.list, memory.list, time.now) and two status memory writes; no use of math/stats/text/workspace.write, no memory retrieval. Most post-first-minute activity followed recorded continuations. n=1; no effort/policy/prompt comparison. Plan usage % not measured. Report docs/experiments/2026-11-15-s011p-hour-001.md.

open_decisions.summary: Select an orchestrator through registered comparisons; earlier local pilots did not establish reliable unguided autonomy.
open_decisions.detail: Evidence in docs/experiments/2026-11-14-orchestrator-candidates.md. llama3.2:3b uses tools most but invents surroundings; qwen3:4b is grounded but needs about 2048 output tokens per reply (hidden reasoning, about 30 s per step); qwen3.5:2b and granite4.1:3b act as assistants waiting for a user. Options: keep llama3.2:3b, adopt qwen3:4b with a larger output limit, authorise a larger partially offloaded model (e.g. qwen3.5:4b or qwen3.5:9b), or enable an external provider (ADR-0005). Worth repeating after S005b, when the world has more tools. Deferred by the human on 2026-11-14: llama3.2:3b stays the default for now. Planned later: try a larger model, and a 'brain swap' mode that can use an external provider with the human's own API key (a frontier model, or a hosted Gemma model) - see the note under S007a in ROADMAP.md. S013 leaves the current default unchanged. Existing approved installed candidates can prove S007a interchangeability without selecting a final research winner. Use registered S007d evidence for the comparison; stronger/offloaded local models require specific download approval. Hosted comparison is optional S007f/S007g with separate credentials, egress and spending gates. S007d-001 tested only the retained Llama default and yielded NO_GO. It does not rank alternatives or change the default. S007h must register one bounded comparison/change with development exposure disclosed. S007h-001 swapped in installed qwen3:4b with all else frozen and also yielded NO_GO (fewer invocations, zero repairs, deadline-bound by hidden reasoning). Neither registered profile is selected as a winner. On 2026-11-15 the owner started the S014 hosted comparison (ADR-0016); hosted arms are compared descriptively, not to pick a default by leaderboard. S007e retained the approved hosted route and installed specialist only; its guided success and partial provider-stopped capability check do not settle orchestrator selection or establish unguided specialist use. S008c statistics engineering and its completed 4-cell capability check add no model-ranking or final orchestrator-selection evidence; the approved gpt-6.1-sol route is retained. S010a portable evidence inventories do not rank models or settle this decision. S010b descriptive comparisons and six source-linked retrospective annotations likewise do not select or rank an orchestrator.
